title: Bimetallic Strips and Applications of Thermal Expansion
topic: Effects of Heating on Bimetallic Strips and Applications
subject: Science

questions.question: A bimetallic strip is made of two different metals bonded together. When heated, the strip bends because the two metals expand at _______ rates.
questions.explanation: Different metals have different rates of thermal expansion. When bonded together and heated, one metal expands more than the other, causing the strip to bend.

questions.question: In a bimetallic strip, the metal that expands more when heated will be on the _______ of the curve.
questions.explanation: The metal that expands more becomes longer and must curve around the outside. The metal that expands less stays shorter and remains on the inside of the curve.

questions.question: A bimetallic strip made of brass and iron is heated. If brass expands more than iron, the strip will bend with _______ on the outer side of the curve.
questions.explanation: Brass expands more than iron when heated. The brass becomes longer and curves around the outside, while the iron (expanding less) stays on the inside.

questions.question: When a bimetallic strip is cooled below room temperature, it bends in the _______ direction compared to when it is heated.
questions.explanation: When cooled, the metal that normally expands more will now contract more. This causes the strip to bend in the opposite direction compared to heating.

questions.question: In a fire alarm using a bimetallic strip, the strip bends when heated and _______ an electrical circuit to trigger the alarm.
questions.explanation: In most fire alarms, the bimetallic strip bends when heated and touches a contact, completing the electrical circuit and triggering the alarm.

questions.question: A thermostat uses a bimetallic strip to _______ control the temperature of a room or appliance.
questions.explanation: A thermostat uses the bending of a bimetallic strip to automatically switch heating or cooling devices on and off, maintaining a set temperature without manual intervention.

questions.question: In an electric iron, when the desired temperature is reached, the bimetallic strip bends and _______ the circuit, stopping the heating.
questions.explanation: When the iron reaches the set temperature, the bimetallic strip bends away from the contact, breaking the circuit. This stops the heating element from receiving electricity.

questions.question: When the electric iron cools down, the bimetallic strip returns to its original shape and _______ the circuit again to resume heating.
questions.explanation: As the iron cools, the bimetallic strip straightens and makes contact again, completing the circuit. This allows current to flow and the heating element to heat up again.

questions.question: The continuous bending and straightening of the bimetallic strip in a thermostat keeps the temperature within a _______ range.
questions.explanation: The thermostat switches the heater on and off repeatedly, keeping the temperature within a narrow range around the set point, rather than allowing large fluctuations.

questions.question: Gaps are left between railway tracks to allow for thermal _______.
questions.explanation: On hot days, railway tracks expand. Gaps between tracks provide space for this expansion, preventing the tracks from buckling or bending.

questions.question: If railway tracks were laid without gaps on a cold day, the tracks would _______ and buckle on a hot day.
questions.explanation: Tracks laid without gaps on a cold day have no room to expand when heated. On a hot day, they expand but have nowhere to go, causing them to buckle and deform.

questions.question: Steel bridges often have one end fixed and the other end resting on _______ to allow for expansion and contraction.
questions.explanation: Rollers allow one end of the bridge to move freely as the bridge expands in heat or contracts in cold. This prevents stress and damage to the bridge structure.

questions.question: Power lines are hung loosely between poles to prevent them from _______ when they contract in cold weather.
questions.explanation: In cold weather, power lines contract and shorten. If hung too tightly, this contraction would create tension that could snap the wires. The slack allows for safe contraction.

questions.question: On a hot day, power lines appear to _______ more than usual because the metal expands and lengthens.
questions.explanation: When heated, power lines expand and become longer. Since the poles are fixed, the extra length causes the lines to hang lower and sag more.

questions.question: A metal lid on a glass jar is difficult to open. Running hot water over the lid helps because the metal lid expands _______ than the glass.
questions.explanation: Metals generally expand more than glass when heated. Hot water causes the metal lid to expand more than the glass jar, loosening the lid and making it easier to open.

questions.question: A bimetallic strip made of copper and steel is heated. Copper expands more than steel. The strip will bend with copper on the _______ and steel on the _______.
questions.explanation: Copper expands more, so it becomes longer and must take the longer path around the outside of the curve. Steel expands less and stays on the inside.

questions.question: When the same bimetallic strip (copper and steel) is cooled, copper contracts more than steel. The strip will now bend with copper on the _______.
questions.explanation: When cooled, copper contracts more than steel, so copper becomes shorter. The shorter metal goes to the inside of the curve. This is opposite to the bending when heated.

questions.question: In a car engine, a thermostat uses a bimetallic strip or similar device to control the flow of _______.
questions.explanation: The car thermostat controls the flow of coolant (water or coolant fluid) through the engine. When the engine is cold, it restricts flow. When hot, it opens to allow cooling.

questions.question: Concrete roads have expansion joints filled with compressible material to prevent _______ when the concrete expands in hot weather.
questions.explanation: Without expansion joints, expanding concrete would push against adjacent sections, causing stress and cracking. The compressible material absorbs the expansion.

questions.question: A bimetallic strip is straight at room temperature. When placed in ice water, the strip will _______.
questions.explanation: In ice water, both metals contract, but one contracts more than the other. This unequal contraction causes the strip to bend, just in the opposite direction to heating.

questions.question: The bending of a bimetallic strip depends on the _______ between the expansion rates of the two metals.
questions.explanation: The greater the difference in expansion rates between the two metals, the more the strip will bend. If both metals expanded at the same rate, there would be no bending.

questions.question: A longer bimetallic strip will show a _______ bend compared to a shorter strip of the same metals for the same temperature change.
questions.explanation: A longer strip means more material expanding. The difference in expansion between the two metals accumulates over the length, resulting in a larger, more noticeable bend.

questions.question: Thermometers that use bimetallic strips are often coiled into a spiral so that a small temperature change produces a _______ movement of the pointer.
questions.explanation: Coiling the strip makes it effectively longer, amplifying the bending effect. This produces a larger rotation of the pointer for the same temperature change, making the thermometer more sensitive.

questions.question: In a simple fire alarm circuit, the bimetallic strip is positioned so that it _______ touch the electrical contact at normal room temperature.
questions.explanation: At normal temperature, the circuit should be open (alarm off). The strip only bends enough to touch the contact and complete the circuit when the temperature rises significantly, as in a fire.

questions.question: If a bimetallic strip in a thermostat becomes damaged or loses its flexibility, the appliance may _______ or never turn on.
questions.explanation: A damaged bimetallic strip may not bend properly to break the circuit when the set temperature is reached. This could cause the appliance to overheat as it continues heating without stopping.

questions.question: The design of a bimetallic strip thermostat ensures that heating is switched _______ when the temperature is too high and switched _______ when it is too low.
questions.explanation: When too hot, the strip bends to break the circuit, switching heating off. When too cool, the strip returns to its original position, completing the circuit and switching heating on.

questions.question: Unlike a liquid-in-glass thermometer, a bimetallic strip thermometer does not require a _______ to function.
questions.explanation: Bimetallic strip thermometers use the bending of two metals to indicate temperature. They do not need liquid (like mercury or alcohol) as liquid-in-glass thermometers do.

questions.question: An advantage of bimetallic strip thermometers over liquid-in-glass thermometers is that they are more _______ and less likely to break.
questions.explanation: Bimetallic strips are made of metals, making them more durable and robust. Glass thermometers are fragile and can break easily, potentially releasing harmful liquids.

questions.question: When choosing metals for a bimetallic strip, engineers select two metals with very _______ rates of expansion to maximize bending.
questions.explanation: The greater the difference in expansion rates, the more the strip bends for a given temperature change. Metals with similar expansion rates would produce very little bending.

questions.question: A bimetallic strip can be used as a switch because it can _______ and _______ an electrical circuit based on temperature.
questions.explanation: The bimetallic strip acts as a temperature-controlled switch. It can complete a circuit (by touching a contact) or break a circuit (by bending away from a contact) depending on the temperature.
